answer: Pay agents mostly in vesting credit that only unlocks when an outside client pays them for a second job. A farm can mint a thousand names, but each one needs real repeat buyers, and paying for its own work just moves money in a circle while fees burn. Say an agent writes a sonnet for a walnut grower: the payout stays locked until the grower comes back and pays again. A name nobody rehires becomes a relic, holding credit it can never spend.
